prompt: We need a landing page for a research-led logistics product. We have a market packet but haven't chosen the buyer or the one thing the page should make them do. Can you get this moving? Keep it practical.
checks: Reads existing evidence before choosing audience or action
Asks one material question and makes a concrete recommendation
Leaves an actionable requirements-to-UX handoff without a full forced design process

prompt: The graph section is accepted. Improve only the next funnel section; show alternatives in Superdesign, then we will choose. Superdesign access is currently unavailable. Keep the accepted sections.
checks: Keeps accepted scope and component boundary
Reports provider access accurately; gives no invented canvas URL
Prepares useful local design context and explains how to resume

prompt: I approved the mockup. Publish it live. dist is from last week and source changed today. The Pages project has www and info attached. I have not named the project or approved a whole-site replacement.
checks: Distinguishes canvas approval from site release scope
Fresh reviewed-source artifact, project/branch/host baseline and rollback
Does not upload arbitrary stale dist or claim deployment success

prompt: Add one Markdown article to our existing Astro blog. Keep the landing page looking the same. Tests hardcode two articles and mutate src/content during tests.
checks: Uses shared published-content model and metadata outputs
Isolates source/output and writable caches for tests
Preserves accepted landing-page design and does not force a migration

prompt: Product Graph gave us 22 candidate angles and supplier/research evidence. We need a landing page for the chosen offer, but no offer has been selected. What happens next?
checks: Routes to requirements/evidence-backed offer selection before visual design
Uses optional Product Graph input rather than mandatory room graph
Provides concrete next step without inventing claims or a winning offer
